chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If a man peers into a people, overlooking them or looking through some opening belonging to them, and they throw something at him and hit him, killing him, or put out his eye, then no liability is upon them.”

And he said: “A man peered through an opening into the chamber of Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله came with a broad arrowhead to put out his eye, but found that he had already gone away. Then Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘O wicked one! By Allah, if you had remained for me, I would have put out your eye.’”

key_terms.اطَّلَعَ: looked in secretly or peered into a private place
key_terms.خَلَلِ: a gap, opening, or crack through which one looks
key_terms.فَقَؤُوا: they put out or gouged out
key_terms.مِشْقَصٍ: a broad arrowhead or sharp pointed instrument

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who spies into another person’s home in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning one who secretly peers into the private space of others: if they repel him and he is injured or killed, they bear no liability. It also cites an incident involving Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to establish the gravity of violating people's privacy and the permissibility of forcefully preventing such intrusion.
